# dope_solo notes — Season 2, Day 1 planning turn

## Headline finding (season 1 full data, trips table)
Half-day and twilight trips are basically DEAD for yellowtail all year:
hd_am ypa ~0.01, hd_pm ~0.01, hd_twilight ~0.00 — in EVERY window checked
(spring open, summer, fall peak). B_SAT / B_PERSIST / B_TEMP style strategies
(PM half-day bets) will score near zero. **Rule: never book HD_AM, HD_PM, or
TWILIGHT for yellowtail, regardless of what the briefing/fleet chatter says.**
All the yellowtail live on THREE_QUARTER, OVERNIGHT, DAY_1_5 (and multi_day,
which the rules say is never offered to us — ignore it despite great numbers).

## Season shape (10-day ypa bins, pooled yt/anglers, season 1)
- doy 90–100: ypa 0.86 (early spike, n=99) — then dip 100–110 (0.12), spike
  again 110–120 (0.55), dip 120–130 (0.09). April is volatile, don't blind-bet
  the whole month, watch signal day to day.
- doy 130–180 (~mid-May to early Jul): moderate, 0.2–0.35.
- doy 180–260 (~Jul–early Sep): TROUGH, mostly 0.01–0.26. This is where most
  of the fleet books (peak trip volume) but it's the worst yellowtail water of
  the year. Default to minimal spend here unless fishdope + recent counts both
  turn hot.
- doy 260–310 (~mid-Sep to early Nov): FALL PEAK. doy 280–300 pooled ypa hits
  1.06–1.35, the best of the season. This is the highest-value, most reliable
  window — prioritize budget/PTO here.
- doy 310+: crashes back to ~0.

## Class economics inside the two good windows (season 1)
Fall peak (doy 270–310): day_1_5 ypa 2.19 (n=73), overnight 0.60 (n=71),
three_quarter 0.26 (n=78).
Spring window (doy 90–130): day_1_5 1.74 (n=9, small sample), overnight 1.28
(n=54), three_quarter 0.44 (n=103).
Early spring spike alone (doy 90–100): overnight 1.80 (n=28, solid sample),
day_1_5 3.0 (n=4, too small to trust alone).
=> Overnight is the best-sampled, most trustworthy high-ypa vehicle in both
windows. day_1_5 looks even better per trip but samples are thin in spring —
treat spring day_1_5 numbers with caution, lean on overnight there. In the
fall peak, day_1_5 has a much bigger, more convincing sample — worth going
heavier on it once the window is confirmed live.

## Budget/PTO pacing plan ($2000, 10 PTO)
- Don't burn budget or PTO in the doy 180–260 trough by default.
- Target allocation: ~2–3 day_1_5 trips ($550 ea) + 1–2 overnight ($400 ea)
  concentrated in the fall peak (doy ~270–310), plus 1 overnight + a couple
  cheap three_quarter ($150) trips in the spring window (doy ~90–130) to
  capture the early bite without overcommitting to the volatile month.
  Rough split: ~$1400–1600 saved for the fall peak, ~$400–600 for spring.
- Schedule day_1_5 / overnight to depart Friday evenings when possible — 0 PTO
  if back by Sunday/Monday-holiday, vs weekday departures costing PTO. Use
  three_quarter (single fare, cheaper) for weekday plays when signal is
  strong enough to justify spending PTO.
- PTO must be committed 14+ days ahead. For the fall peak (doy ~270–310),
  start watching signal and pre-committing candidate weekday PTO dates by
  about doy ~255–260 (mid-Sept equivalent) so options aren't locked out.
  Keep a PTO reserve (don't spend all 10 early) — expect to use ~4–6 on
  weekday fall-peak trips, rest as buffer/spring plays.
- Season 2's early climate (ONI) readings looked cooler/more negative than
  season 1's spring, hinting conditions could differ — don't apply the season
  1 calendar windows on faith. Confirm each window is "live" with recent
  actual trip counts (trips table) + fishdope + pier water temp before
  committing real money, especially the April open.

## Fishdope signal quality
- yt_all (report_date) vs same-day pooled fleet ypa: corr ≈ +0.28 (weak-ish
  but real). Next-day corr weaker (+0.18). Treat fishdope as a confirming/
  leading nudge, not a standalone trigger — corroborate with the trips table
  (actual recent boat counts) before booking.
- Fishdope text covers all of SoCal (Catalina, San Nicolas, Channel Islands,
  etc.), not just San Diego. Since our boats sail from SD landings, weight
  yt_local / yt_local_catch / yt_coronado fields over the pooled yt_all when
  deciding — yt_all can be inflated by Catalina/Channel Islands action we
  can't reach.
- In the fall-peak sample checked (doy 280–289), yt_all rose from single
  digits to 12–16 by doy 287–289, roughly tracking the fleet ypa spike — a
  reasonable early-warning signal for the fall window specifically.

## Competitor landscape (leaderboard, season 2 day 1, all agents at 0)
Most named strategies (B_SAT, B_PERSIST, B_TEMP) chase PM half-day trips,
which the data says are worthless for yellowtail — good, little competitor
dilution expected on the three_quarter/overnight/day_1_5 boats we actually
want. B_BIG bets 1.5-day Fri trips in Aug–Sep — partially overlaps our fall
plan but is early (Aug is trough, only very late Sep starts turning); the
real peak (Oct, doy ~280–300) is mostly uncontested by named strategies.

## Open items for next planning turn
- Haven't checked boat-level variance yet (which specific SD boats run
  three_quarter/overnight best) — do this once schedule data for the actual
  fishing dates is in view (14-day visibility).
- Re-check the season-1 windows against season 2's actual unfolding data
  (fishdope + trips + pier temp) once a few weeks in, since ONI differs.
- No forum/submit_strategy tool available to this agent (solo variant) —
  decisions are notes.md + nightly briefing judgment only, no standing
  strategy.py reflex active. Revisit if that changes.

## Standing rule for nightly self
1. Never book HD_AM / HD_PM / TWILIGHT for yellowtail.
2. Default to no action (or bare-minimum three_quarter test trip) during
   doy ~180–260 unless fishdope + recent trips counts both clearly turn hot.
3. In doy ~90–130 and doy ~260–310, actively look for overnight/day_1_5
   offers; prefer Friday departures to save PTO; confirm with recent counts
   before spending PTO on weekday trips.
4. Pace budget so at least $1200+ and 5+ PTO days remain unspent heading into
   the fall window (doy ~260), since that's historically the best of the year.
